question: Does PIRS introduce a novel 3D-RES core mechanism, or is mask-IoU-derived referent-score supervision already established in the original sources?

sources.title: Superpoint Transformer for 3D Scene Instance Segmentation
sources.finding: SPFormer's shared prediction head predicts an IoU-aware score for each query, and its score branch estimates the IoU between the predicted superpoint mask and the ground-truth mask. The training loss is an L2 target ||s_k - iou_k||_2 on assigned high-quality proposals, and the score is used in the final ranking score sqrt(p_i * s_i * ms_i).

sources.title: RG-SAN: Rule-Guided Spatial Awareness Network for End-to-End 3D Referring Expression Segmentation
sources.finding: RG-SAN is a 3D-RES method on ScanRefer and explicitly adds an auxiliary score loss for mask-quality prediction, citing SPFormer. This imports the mask-IoU-derived classification-score mechanism into the exact task family.

sources.title: RefMask3D: Language-Guided Transformer for 3D Referring Segmentation
sources.finding: The full source uses Hungarian matching and matched-object classification/mask losses. It does not remove SPFormer/RG-SAN prior art for score targets derived from mask IoU.

sources.title: 3D-STMN: Dependency-Driven Superpoint-Text Matching Network for End-to-End 3D Referring Expression Segmentation
sources.finding: The original source establishes dense superpoint-text matching through a different mechanism; it does not clear the mask-quality-score prior art above.

sources.title: 3D-GRES: Generalized 3D Referring Expression Segmentation
sources.finding: The paper defines query target-presence BCE and query-text alignment; it does not establish a novel distinction that rescues PIRS, and its own multi-query mechanism is orthogonal prior art.

sources.title: LESS: Label-Efficient and Single-Stage Referring 3D Segmentation
sources.finding: LESS uses query-mask and query-sentence alignment with binary-mask supervision. It is additional 3D-RES prior art and does not restore novelty to a generic mask-quality score target.

verdict.literature_gate: fail for a new core mechanism
verdict.reason: Mask-IoU-derived query-quality supervision is already explicit in SPFormer and is already applied to ScanRefer 3D-RES by RG-SAN. PIRS changes the assignment/supervision unit to detached soft targets on every query, but the core mechanism remains prior art rather than a distinct whole-mechanism contribution.
verdict.disposition: Keep M197-PIRS running to terminate the already-admitted experiment and preserve its pre-registered evidence, but admit no successor and leave the one design-budget slot empty. A future candidate must change the causal mechanism rather than rename or retune this quality-target idea.

limitations: This is a bounded audit of six primary 3D vision/referring-segmentation sources plus the earlier VarifocalNet check; it is not an exhaustive literature proof.
The source archives were fetched from the versioned arXiv e-print URLs and hashed locally; the archive hashes are recorded above.
The audit establishes prior art for the core score-target mechanism and does not claim that PIRS has no incremental implementation differences.
